Unfreezes the three axe-core WCAG audits in accessibility.spec.js. A live
axe run revealed the actual violations differed from the stale TODO:

- aria-required-children: dropped the redundant ARIA menubar/menuitem/menu
  roles from navbar.html (the <nav aria-label> landmark already provides
  navigation semantics; a menubar requires menuitem children, which the
  search/settings buttons were not) and added role="tab" to the
  theme-preview disabled tab so its tablist is valid
- link-name: aria-label on the site-subtitle home link (its text span can
  be CSS-hidden); aria-label on an icon-only demo button
- list: admin/footer separator kept as a list item (aria-hidden <hr>)
  instead of role="separator" which broke the list's required children
- scrollable-region-focusable: code blocks are now a single focusable

default/section/news layouts already use a <main> landmark — so pages built on

display:block like <div>, so there is no visual change.

SEO/structured-content, and AI/crawler main-content extraction — engines can
isolate primary content from header/nav/footer chrome.

* feat(scripts): add dependency-free preview-image pixelator

Add a utility that pixelates and palette-quantizes the AI-generated preview
banners into indexed PNG-8, shrinking them ~90% while preserving the retro
8-bit aesthetic. A dry-run across all 146 banners reports 283MB -> 28MB.

The preview art is intentionally "retro pixel art / 8-bit" styling, so
downsampling and reducing the colour palette both shrink the files and
reinforce the intended look.

  fast (~3s per 1536x1024 banner). Supports --dry-run, --jobs parallelism,
  --block/--scale/--max-width, --backup, --force, and --selftest.
- scripts/features/pixelate-preview-images: conventions-friendly bash wrapper
  that defaults to preview_images.output_dir from _config.yml and forwards
  flags to the engine.
- scripts/pixelate-preview-images.sh: back-compat wrapper.
- scripts/test/lib/test_pixelate_images.sh: round-trip + dry-run + graceful
  non-PNG handling tests, wired into the library test runner.

subject: fix(chat-proxy): identify as Claude Code for subscription OAuth tokens (#185)
body:
Claude subscription OAuth tokens (`claude setup-token` / rotating refresh) are
gated to Claude Code: the Messages API requires the FIRST system block to
identify as Claude Code, otherwise it rejects the request with a misleading
`429 rate_limit_error` (terse `"message":"Error"`). The proxy forwarded the
chat's custom system prompt and never identified as Claude Code, so every
OAuth-mode request — local dev AND the deployed Cloudflare Worker — was rejected.

handleChat now prepends "You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for
Claude." as the first system block in OAuth modes (oauth_static / oauth_refresh),
keeping the site assistant's own instructions as a second block. API-key mode is
unchanged.

Verified end-to-end via the live widget: the identical request returned 429
before and a real streamed, page-grounded answer after. Adds a README note
documenting the gate.

body:
* test: add unit tests for content-review.rb scoring engine (#166)

scripts/content-review.rb (the deterministic content-review tier) had zero
direct unit coverage — it only ran as a side effect of the ai-content-review
workflow. A scoring regression (code-fence false-positive) already shipped and
was fixed in v1.18.1 (#155), exactly the class of bug a unit test catches.

New scripts/test/lib/test_content_review.sh drives the reviewer against
synthetic Markdown fixtures using the REAL production config + schema (so the
tested thresholds can't drift from a copy). Asserts:
  - a well-formed docs page scores >= 80,
  - removing the required `description` lowers the score and reports the issue,
  - a closing bare ``` after a language-tagged fence is not flagged
    (the v1.18.1 regression guard),
  - --strict exits non-zero below the fail threshold; warn mode exits 0.

Fixtures live under a temp pages/_docs/** tree so the production scope and
path-pattern globs match without touching real content. Runs under LC_ALL=C

  optional route (string) + depends_on ([T-NNN]) fields.
- backlog.yml schema header documents adoption + the new optional fields.

non-destructive upsert), and a real-gh --dry-run adopting issue #204

* chore(config): preload Jekyll gems in devcontainer for fast Codespaces launch

Build the devcontainer from the repo's own docker/Dockerfile `dev-test`
stage instead of the generic MS Jekyll image. That stage runs
`bundle install` at image-build time, so every gem is baked into the
image — no full `bundle install` on each Codespace create, and the gems
always match the checked-out branch's Gemfile.lock. With Codespaces
prebuilds enabled, launch becomes near-instant.

- Drop the docker-in-docker and node features (not needed to render the
  site; Playwright/Sass run on the host) to keep create + prebuild fast.
- postCreateCommand is now `bundle check || bundle install` (fast no-op
  when gems are preloaded; self-heals only on lock drift).
- Auto-serve uses nohup + --force_polling (reliable watching over the
  Codespaces bind mount) and logs to /tmp/jekyll-serve.log.
- No workspaceMount/workspaceFolder override: Codespaces always mounts at
  /workspaces/<repo> and gems live at the global /usr/local/bundle, so
  bundle exec works from the default folder (max compatibility).
- Run as root to match the ruby:3.3-slim base and docker-compose, avoiding
  gem/bind-mount permission friction.

Add .devcontainer/README.md documenting the design and how to enable
prebuilds, and update the devcontainer docs page to match.

subject: feat(automation): verify-and-close lane — autopilot closes human issues fixed on main when CI is green (#247)
body:
Today the issue autopilot can never close a human-authored issue: the engine
downgrades any close disposition to needs-human, and the only deterministic
close path is bot-noise (`eligible_autoclose`). The recurring cost is "zombie"
issues — bugs/features already fixed on `main` that stay open and get
re-surfaced every pass until a maintainer closes them by hand.

Add a verify-and-close lane that closes a human issue only on hard evidence,
gated by CI/CD:

- triage.py flags every non-protected, non-epic human issue `verify_candidate`

  for humans is unchanged — a human issue is still never closed as "stale").
- issue-verifier (new, read-only agent) judges whether each candidate's fix is
  ALREADY on `main` and writes verdicts (with file:line evidence) to
  .issues/verify.json. It never closes/comments/labels/merges/edits.
- verify_close.py is the deterministic gate: it closes a verdict's issue only
  when resolved + high-confidence + a genuine verify_candidate AND `main`'s

  API error, pending run, or failure.

subject: fix(ci): make claude-run truly OAuth-first — drop API key whenever an OAuth token is set (#248)
body:
The action advertises "OAuth-first", but its guard only unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
when the API key was ALREADY empty:

    if [ -n "$CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN" ] && [ -z "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; fi

So when BOTH a real OAuth token and a real API key are present, the Claude CLI
authenticates with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — the OAuth token never wins. With the
repo's API-key account out of credit, every agent step fails "Credit balance is
too low" even though the intent is to bill the Claude subscription via OAuth.

Drop ANTHROPIC_API_KEY whenever an OAuth token is set, so OAuth is the genuine
default and a present-but-credit-less API key can't shadow it. The no-auth no-op
and API-key-only fallback are unchanged (verified by a 4-case simulation).

NOTE: a CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret must still be configured for this to take
effect (`claude setup-token` → `gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`); today the
repo has only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
